purpose: The application settings record, replayed. Each case carries the op (without the schema wrapper) and the answer the kernel must give: the parsed answer, or {"error": "<the exact Err string>"} when the request itself is malformed. ds-web replays the same file through the vendored WASM, so no default, bound, first-launch rule, legacy-lane migration or lane decision can be true on one host and not another.
source: Transcribed from ds-web src/lib/stores/applicationSettings.ts (DEFAULT_APPLICATION_SETTINGS, every normalize* helper, normalizeSettings, loadApplicationSettings, updateApplicationSettings, resetApplicationSettings, mapPerformanceProfileForBudget, workingAreaUpdateIntervalLabel), src/lib/batch/browser-bulk.ts (normalizeBrowserBatchConcurrency), src/lib/stores/processingLane.ts (standardLaneAvailable, normalizeLane, setProcessingLane), and every case of src/tests/application-settings.test.ts and the store cases of src/tests/processing-lane.test.ts, 2026-09-12.
note: Re-record expected with DS_APPLICATION_SETTINGS_CASES_WRITE=1 cargo test --test application_settings_cases after a deliberate rule change, and say why in the commit.

cases.why: A fresh install with nothing saved answers DEFAULT_APPLICATION_SETTINGS key for key, in the store's order, with the desktop's device defaults; nothing is written back.

On a phone the first launch reads popupMode minimal and the My Location control on, from the device facts alone; first_launch says so and persist stays false because the device recomputes the same default next launch.
A persisted popupMode and showMyLocationControl are the operator's explicit choice: a phone does not override them and first_launch reports neither.
A blob carrying popupMode null was never chosen (`== null`), so the device default applies exactly as for an absent key.
The SSR and desktop-safe My Location default is off; an explicit false in the blob is kept even where the device would default it on.
`{...saved}` over a string spreads no setting: a corrupt blob reads as an empty one — defaults and a first launch — rather than a refusal, because a saved blob is user data.
A retired key (showImageRotationInProperties) or any unknown key in the persisted blob normalises away while the supported keys beside it are kept.
The oldest lane record was a bare string under ds_processing_lane; with no processingLane in the blob it migrates and the store writes the merged record back once.
The later lane record was {lane}; it migrates the same way and is written back the same way.
A legacy Standard carries no confirmation marker, so the migrated record reads fast — and the migration is still written, exactly as the store wrote it.
processing-lane.test 'ignores unknown stored values': {lane:'unknown'} is truthy, so it migrates, normalises to fast, and the store wrote that back.
A blob that already carries a processingLane is never overwritten by the legacy record, and nothing is written back.
A confirmed Standard preference in the blob is kept with its marker; the legacy fast record is ignored and persist stays false.
`!saved?.processingLane` is a truthiness test: an unreadable but truthy saved lane blocks the migration and normalises to fast without a write-back.
An empty legacy string is falsy: nothing migrates and nothing is written back.
A legacy record with no lane key, or a value that is neither a string nor an object, yields no lane (`legacyLane?.lane` is undefined).
A number under the legacy key has no `.lane` and is not a string, so it is not a lane.
processing-lane.test 'falls back to fast when stored standard mode was never confirmed': Standard needs its confirmation marker or it is fast.
processing-lane.test 'restores standard mode only with confirmation metadata': the marker rides with the preference and a stale fast marker is dropped.
processing-lane.test 'restores fast mode when the setting carries an explicit confirmation marker': the deprecated fast marker is carried while fast is the preference.
A whitespace-only marker is not a timestamp (`value.trim()` is falsy), so Standard is not confirmed and reads fast without a marker.

Each numeric setting above its ceiling lands exactly on it: zooms 22, exaggeration 100, gap 10000, corridor 500, terrain gap 5000, clearance and drop 100, opacity 1, strokes 8, point 24, grid 100000, GPS 300, budget 5, concurrency 100, working area 1440.

Each numeric setting below its floor lands exactly on it: zooms 0, exaggeration 0.5, gap 0 (a rounded 0.4), corridor 1, terrain gap 1, clearance and drop 0, opacity 0.05, strokes 0.5, point 1, grid 0.1, GPS 1, budget 1, concurrency 1, working area 15.
The profile normalisers that demand a positive (or non-negative) value take their default for zero or negative input, and a non-positive grid interval is the adaptive null.
application-settings.test: '4.4' → 4, '3.6' → 4, '15' → 15, '250' → 250; a stored string reads through Number() exactly as the store read it.
Math.round takes halves up: '4.5' → 5, 2.5 → 3, 6.25 m → 6.3, 1.125 px → 1.25, 2.25 px → 2.5, opacity 0.125 → 0.13; the batch concurrency floors instead (7.9 → 7).
application-settings.test: 'bad' → the default for the budget (3), the GPS interval (1) and the working area (never); every other numeric key does the same.

Number('') is 0: an empty zoom reads 0, an empty budget and GPS interval clip to 1, an empty alignment gap is 0, while the working area, the grid interval and the batch concurrency treat blank as their default.
Number(null) is 0: the profile keys read without a `??` guard land on 0 (or the floor above it) for null, while the guarded keys — zooms, GPS, budget, concurrency, working area — take their default.
application-settings.test: 'never' is no background refresh and 'auto' is the adaptive grid interval; 60 and 90 minutes are kept as given.
application-settings.test: 60 → 60 and 90 → 90 are opt-in intervals inside the range and are not snapped to the option list.
Number() accepts 0x, 0o, 0b and exponent forms and 'Infinity' (which is not finite, so the working area falls to never); the reading is the browser's, not a stricter one.
application-settings.test: 'bad' placement → bottom-left, 'all' grid label → top-left; an unknown popup mode, fill mode or lane word takes its default too.
application-settings.test: 'cursor', 'top-right' and 'bottom-right' are accepted placements; 'none' hides grid labels; 'to_clearance' fills to the clearance line; 'minimal' is the phone card.
A profile colour is a trimmed #rrggbb, lower-cased; 'invalid', a short form or a non-string takes the default.
application-settings.test 'migrates the earlier blue-tinted terrain defaults': #94a3b8 and #38bdf8 as the terrain point colour become #d1d5db.
The first short-lived terrain default was the ground blue itself; as a terrain point colour it migrates while the ground keeps it.
application-settings.test 'de-duplicates hidden side profiles': ' side-a ' is side-a, '' is dropped; a number, null or boolean item becomes its JavaScript string as the store's map(String) made it.
The hidden id list is bounded to 500 after trimming and de-duplication, so a runaway blob cannot grow the record without limit.
A string or object under hiddenProfileAlignmentIds is not a list of ids; it reads as the empty default.
A flag is read only from a JSON boolean: 'false', 0 and 1 are not choices and take the default, while an explicit false is kept.
profileTerrainPointWidthPx was once persisted as profileTerrainPointRadiusPx; the old key is read only when the new one is null or absent.
When both the width and the retired radius key are present the width is the value and the radius is ignored.
The parity baseline: a record the store already normalised and persisted reopens key for key and value for value, so an existing profile is not rewritten by the move.
processing-lane.test 'withholds standard when the active project does not support it, without rewriting the setting': the record keeps Standard, the lane answered is fast.
processing-lane.test 'forces fast in the installed app even for a stored, confirmed standard setting': the installed shell is fast-only by ruling and the preference is not rewritten.
A host that has no lane facts at boot gets the record without a lane; the lane is asked separately through the lane op.
application-settings.test 'ignores unknown persisted-shaped keys while retaining supported settings': the retired and unknown keys vanish, showZoomLevelReadout is kept.
application-settings.test 'defaults to Fast and requires confirmation metadata for Standard': a bare processingLane 'standard' patch does not change the lane.
The same test's second step: Standard with its confirmation marker is the preference and the marker is carried in the record.
The same test's last step: patching processingLane fast over a confirmed Standard drops standardLaneConfirmedAt.
JSON has no undefined: a null in the patch clears the key exactly as `{...current, key: undefined}` did, so clearing the Standard marker drops the lane to fast.

The host sends null for the store's undefined on ANY key, not only a marker; `{...current, key: undefined}` gave every reader its default, so the null removes the key before reading — a merged null would be Number(null), 0, on the keys the store did not guard with ??, and a stroke width would clip to 0.5 instead of the shipped 1.5.
application-settings.test 'normalizes profile styles and de-duplicates hidden side profiles': 250 → 100 m, invalid colour → default, 30 px → 8, 0 px → 1, opacity 2 → 1, ids deduplicated.
application-settings.test 'migrates the earlier blue-tinted terrain defaults to neutral light gray': #94a3b8 → #d1d5db; a following patch to #e5e7eb is kept (next case).
The second half of the migration test: a colour that is not one of the two retired defaults is kept as given.
application-settings.test 'shows the grid and snaps to it by default, and both stay togglable': both flags default on and both accept false.
application-settings.test 'keeps hover popups fixed bottom-left by default and accepts other placements': bottom-right is accepted and the popups can be disabled.
application-settings.test 'keeps the SSR and desktop-safe My Location default off and persists overrides': setting the control on over the default is kept.
The current record is read through the same normaliser as the patch, so a stale key or an out-of-range value already in the store cannot survive a change.
With lane facts in the request the patched record's effective lane rides in the same answer: a confirmed Standard on a fast-only project is fast.
application-settings.test 'restores only the named keys and leaves every other setting untouched': budget and GPS interval return to 3 and 1, the exaggeration 7 survives.
application-settings.test 'resets device-aware defaults to a device value, never to a placeholder': on a phone popupMode is minimal and the My Location control is on.
The same reset on a desktop lands on normal and off — exactly where a fresh install there would, not on a value the device class would override.
A confirmation marker has no shipped default, so resetting it clears it and Standard is no longer confirmed.
An empty key list is a no-op: the current record comes back normalised and otherwise as it was.
The key list is host-authored, not user data: a name that is not a setting is a bug in the host and an Err, not a silent no-op.

expected.error: reset names settings that do not exist: bogus

cases.why: processing-lane.test 'persists standard in IndexedDB and scopes it to processing routes': on deployed web with a supporting project a confirmed Standard is Standard.
The active project must declare Standard in its processing_lanes property; absent, the lane is fast and the preference is untouched.
processing-lane.test 'offers the standard lane on web and withholds it in the installed app': the installed shell is fast-only by ruling (2026-08-13).
The record is normalised before the lane is read, so a raw blob claiming Standard without its marker cannot reach the Standard lane.
processing-lane.test 'defaults processing calls to the fast path': nothing saved is fast everywhere.
processing-lane.test 'restores fast mode from stored settings without a confirmation marker': fast is fast even where Standard is offered.
setProcessingLane('standard') where Standard is reachable writes the preference with the confirmation time and clears the deprecated fast marker.

The write path refuses through the same seam: on the installed shell a requested Standard is written as fast with no marker, so a desktop operator can never select Standard, see it selected, and silently get Fast.
A project that does not declare Standard withholds it at the write path too.
setProcessingLane('fast') writes fast and clears standardLaneConfirmedAt; a fast marker already in the record is left as it was.
The clock is an input; a blank confirmation time would write a Standard that immediately reads as fast, so the request is refused as malformed.
application-settings.test 'maps lower budgets to tighter MapLibre cache profiles': budget 1 keeps 48 tiles, cleans up after 120 ms and does not refresh expired tiles.

profile.label: Saver
profile.description: Small tile cache and quicker cleanup for low-memory browsers.

cases.why: The other half of the same test: budget 5 keeps 384 tiles, cleans up after 1000 ms and refreshes expired tiles.

profile.label: Maximum
profile.description: Keeps more tiles resident for large screens and high-memory devices.

cases.why: application-settings.test 'raises the top tile cache on capable browser resource estimates': a 4 GiB heap limit is 'Capable browser estimate' and 384 × 4/3 rounds to 512 tiles.

profile.label: Maximum
profile.description: Keeps more tiles resident for large screens and high-memory devices.

cases.why: 8 GB of device memory is the 'Large browser estimate' at scale 1.5: the balanced 160 becomes 240 tiles.

profile.label: Balanced
profile.description: Default cache budget for everyday project editing.

cases.why: 2 GB of device memory is the 'Constrained browser estimate' at scale 0.75: 48 × 0.75 = 36 rounds to 32 tiles, above the 24-tile floor.

profile.label: Saver
profile.description: Small tile cache and quicker cleanup for low-memory browsers.

cases.why: hardwareConcurrency of 8 or more is 'Capable' on its own; a string count reads through Number() like the rest.

profile.label: Low
profile.description: Keeps memory tight while preserving normal map navigation.

cases.why: An unreadable budget is the default 3 (Balanced), and no hint at all is the standard estimate.

profile.label: Balanced
profile.description: Default cache budget for everyday project editing.

cases.why: application-settings.test 'labels supported intervals plainly': null is 'Never'.
application-settings.test 'labels supported intervals plainly': 15 is '15 min'.
application-settings.test 'labels supported intervals plainly': 60 is '1 hour', singular.
application-settings.test 'labels supported intervals plainly': 90 is '1 hour 30 min'.
application-settings.test 'labels supported intervals plainly': 1440 is '24 hours', plural.
The label is of the normalised interval: 5 clips to 15 min and an unreadable value is Never.
An op the contract does not name is the host's bug: an Err, not an answer.

expected.error: invalid application settings request: unknown variant `sideways`, expected one of `normalize`, `patch`, `reset`, `lane`, `set_lane`, `performance_profile`, `interval_label` at line 1 column 62

cases.why: The request envelope is strict even though the blob inside it is lenient: an extra field in the op is refused.

expected.error: invalid application settings request: unknown field `extra`, expected one of `saved`, `legacy_lane`, `device`, `lane_facts` at line 1 column 141

cases.why: The lane op needs both facts; without them there is no lane to answer.

expected.error: invalid application settings request: missing field `lane_facts` at line 1 column 74

cases.why: A patch is an object of changes; a string is not one.

expected.error: invalid application settings request: invalid type: string "x", expected a map at line 1 column 86

cases.why: Another schema version is refused by name so a host built against a later contract cannot be answered by this one.

expected.error: unsupported application settings schema; expected ds.application-settings/v1
